-- ref GlobalStrings.lua — the eight labels (enUS), in the `X = X or` FALLBACK form: the -- app runs the real localized GlobalStrings.lua off the patch chain BEFORE this file -- (ui_script/mod.rs load_global_strings), so the installed locale wins and these copies -- only fill in for the test harnesses, which load no patch chain. CombatText.xml's shape. CHARACTER_BUTTON = CHARACTER_BUTTON or "Character Info" SPELLBOOK_ABILITIES_BUTTON = SPELLBOOK_ABILITIES_BUTTON or "Spellbook & Abilities" TALENTS_BUTTON = TALENTS_BUTTON or "Talents" QUESTLOG_BUTTON = QUESTLOG_BUTTON or "Quest Log" SOCIAL_BUTTON = SOCIAL_BUTTON or "Social" WORLDMAP_BUTTON = WORLDMAP_BUTTON or "World Map" MAINMENU_BUTTON = MAINMENU_BUTTON or "Main Menu" HELP_BUTTON = HELP_BUTTON or "Help Request"
-- ...and their second lines, ref GlobalStrings.lua l.2722/2766/2768/2758/2765/2788/2747/2739, -- verbatim (enUS). 1.12 ships detailed tooltips ON (decision 0661), so every one of these is -- part of the default hover, not an opt-in extra. NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_CHARACTER = NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_CHARACTER or "Information about your character, including equipment, statistics, skills, and reputation." NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_SPELLBOOK = NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_SPELLBOOK or "All of your spells and abilities. To move a spell or ability to your Action Bar, open the Spellbook & Abilities window, left-click that spell or ability, and drag it down to your Action Bar." NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_TALENTS = NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_TALENTS or "The array of talents available to enhance and specialize your character." NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_QUESTLOG = NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_QUESTLOG or "A list of all the active quests you currently have. You can have up to 20 active quests at one time." NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_SOCIAL = NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_SOCIAL or "Information about other people in the game. You can use the Social window to manage your friends list and ignore list, as well as see who is online." NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_WORLDMAP = NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_WORLDMAP or "As you explore a zone, more areas of interest will become visible on the world map. You can use left-click to zoom in, or right-click to zoom out." NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_MAINMENU = NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_MAINMENU or "Here you can modify your video, sound, and interface settings, or create custom hotkeys. You can also choose to log out or exit the program altogether." NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_HELP = NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_HELP or "Through this menu, you can report a bug. You can also use the Help Request menu to talk to one of our Game Masters (GMs) in the game if you have questions or need assistance."
-- ref LoadMicroButtonTextures (MainMenuBarMicroButtons.lua l.1-9): the Up/Down/Disabled trio -- under one art name plus the shared highlight. `art` is nil for CharacterMicroButton, whose -- textures don't follow the pattern (UI-MicroButtonCharacter-*, and no Disabled variant -- exists in the archives) — it sets its own. -- `newbie` is the ref's per-button `this.newbieText` (set in each button's own OnLoad there — -- MainMenuBarMicroButtons.lua l.95 and .xml l.101/127/149/174/193/215); Spellbook is the one -- the ref hands to the call site instead, because its label swaps with GetSpellBookState. function BenillaMicroButton_OnLoad(button, art, label, binding, newbie) button.label = label button.binding = binding button.newbieText = newbie -- Seat over the bar plate (ActionBar.xml's helper, which carries the why). Called -- nil-guarded for the same reason BagFrame.xml's two calls are: the shipped load order -- always has the bar first, but a test harness may load this file alone — and with no -- bar there is nothing to seat above. if BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove then BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove(button) end if art then local prefix = "Interface\\Buttons\\UI-MicroButton-" .. art button:SetNormalTexture(prefix .. "-Up") button:SetPushedTexture(prefix .. "-Down") button:SetDisabledTexture(prefix .. "-Disabled") end button:SetHighlightTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\UI-MicroButton-Hilight") button:RegisterForClicks("LeftButtonUp", "RightButtonUp") end
-- ref MicroButtonTooltipText (l.11-18) with a static binding label — see the SCOPE note. -- Benilla-named, not the ref global: the ref's takes (text, bindingAction) and looks the key -- up live, so reusing that name for a different contract would be a trap for the next -- ref-quoted transcription that calls it. function BenillaMicroButton_TooltipText(button) if button.binding then return button.label .. " " .. NORMAL_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. "(" .. button.binding .. ")" .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE end return button.label end
-- ref MainMenuBarMicroButton's OnEnter (l.13), verbatim bar the owner shift: -- GameTooltip_AddNewbieTip(this.tooltipText, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, this.newbieText) function BenillaMicroButton_OnEnter(button) if not GameTooltip_AddNewbieTip then return end -- engine tests load file subsets GameTooltip_AddNewbieTip(button, BenillaMicroButton_TooltipText(button), 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, button.newbieText) end
-- Is a panel up? `getglobal` because every panel this asks about loads AFTER this file — -- the first UpdateMicroButtons can land before most of them exist. function BenillaMicro_PanelShown(name) local frame = getglobal(name) return frame ~= nil and frame:IsVisible() end
function BenillaMicroButton_SetPushed(button, isPushed) if not button then return end if isPushed then button:SetButtonState("PUSHED") else button:SetButtonState("NORMAL") end end
-- ref UpdateMicroButtons (l.20-84): each button reflects whether its panel is up. The -- MainMenu arm is the ref's own six-way test (l.47-58) minus the five frames that don't -- exist here — GameMenuFrame is the one that does (decision 0674), and it is the one the -- reference lists first. Its keyring arm has no frame here; the still-unwired Help button -- simply never pushes. function UpdateMicroButtons() BenillaMicroButton_SetPushed(CharacterMicroButton, BenillaMicro_PanelShown("BenillaCharacterFrame")) BenillaMicroButton_SetPushed(SpellbookMicroButton, BenillaMicro_PanelShown("BenillaSpellBookFrame")) BenillaMicroButton_SetPushed(TalentMicroButton, BenillaMicro_PanelShown("BenillaTalentFrame")) BenillaMicroButton_SetPushed(QuestLogMicroButton, BenillaMicro_PanelShown("BenillaQuestLogFrame")) BenillaMicroButton_SetPushed(WorldMapMicroButton, BenillaMicro_PanelShown("WorldMapFrame")) BenillaMicroButton_SetPushed(MainMenuMicroButton, BenillaMicro_PanelShown("GameMenuFrame")) end
-- ref CharacterMicroButton_SetPushed/_SetNormal (l.109-117): the portrait shifts its window -- and dims while the button is down. The window is a TexCoord crop of the SAME "player" -- portrait bake the unit frame samples (SetPortraitTexture below) — the round stencil lives -- in the bake's own UV space, so cropping it yields the ref's rectangular slice of a masked -- face rather than an ellipse fitted to this 18x25 region. function CharacterMicroButton_SetPushed() MicroButtonPortrait:SetTexCoord(0.2666, 0.8666, 0, 0.8333) MicroButtonPortrait:SetAlpha(0.5) end
function CharacterMicroButton_SetNormal() MicroButtonPortrait:SetTexCoord(0.2, 0.8, 0.0666, 0.9) MicroButtonPortrait:SetAlpha(1.0) end
-- ref CharacterMicroButton's OnUpdate (its XML l.55-61) drives the portrait off the live -- button state — which is what makes the face dim mid-mouse-hold, a thing UpdateMicroButtons -- can't see. Transcribed, but EDGE-TRIGGERED: the ref re-applies both setters every frame; -- there is no reason to re-push identical TexCoord/alpha 60x a second. function CharacterMicroButton_OnUpdate(button) local pushed = (button:GetButtonState() == "PUSHED") if pushed ~= button.portraitPushed then button.portraitPushed = pushed if pushed then CharacterMicroButton_SetPushed() else CharacterMicroButton_SetNormal() end end end
function CharacterMicroButton_OnLoad(button) -- The player's face, from the same portrait slot the unit frame binds (portrait/mod.rs -- keeps the "player" entry live across re-bakes, so unlike the ref there is no -- UNIT_PORTRAIT_UPDATE re-bind to register — the binding is by token, not by handle). SetPortraitTexture(MicroButtonPortrait, "player") button:SetNormalTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\UI-MicroButtonCharacter-Up") button:SetPushedTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\UI-MicroButtonCharacter-Down") BenillaMicroButton_OnLoad(button, nil, CHARACTER_BUTTON, "C", NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_CHARACTER) end
-- ref UpdateTalentButton (l.133-141): no talents before level 10, so the button goes away -- and the row closes up behind it. Guarded on BOTH frames: it re-anchors the quest-log -- button, which is created after the talent one, so the very first call has to be able to -- land before the row is fully built. (`UnitLevel` answers 0, never nil, for a unit the -- client hasn't got yet — so pre-login the button is simply hidden until the level lands.) function UpdateTalentButton() if not TalentMicroButton or not QuestLogMicroButton then return end if UnitLevel("player") < 10 then TalentMicroButton:Hide() QuestLogMicroButton:SetPoint("BOTTOMLEFT", "TalentMicroButton", "BOTTOMLEFT", 0, 0) else TalentMicroButton:Show() QuestLogMicroButton:SetPoint("BOTTOMLEFT", "TalentMicroButton", "BOTTOMRIGHT", -3, 0) end end
function TalentMicroButton_OnLoad(button) BenillaMicroButton_OnLoad(button, "Talents", TALENTS_BUTTON, "N", NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_TALENTS) button:RegisterEvent("UNIT_LEVEL") button:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD") end
function TalentMicroButton_OnEvent() -- UNIT_LEVEL names its unit in arg1; every other unit's ding is none of our business. if event == "UNIT_LEVEL" and arg1 ~= "player" then return end UpdateTalentButton() end
